slides.heading: Merging Linked Lists
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Medium · Linked Lists
slides.narration: Let's solve Merging Linked Lists, a medium linked lists problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Two lists may converge into a shared tail; return the first shared node or null.
Two pointers that switch lists meet at the junction after at most n+m steps.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Two lists may converge into a shared tail; return the first shared node or null. Two pointers that switch lists meet at the junction after at most n plus m steps.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Two pointers that switch to the other list after finishing travel the same distance and meet at the junction.
slides.narration: Two pointers that switch to the other list after finishing travel the same distance and meet at the junction.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Brute force: for each A node, scan B → O(n·m)
Hash set of A nodes → O(n + m) time, O(n) space
Two pointers switching lists → O(1) space
slides.narration: Comparing every pair is quadratic. A hash set of A's nodes is linear but uses memory. Two pointers that switch to the other list at the end both travel the same total distance, so they meet at the intersection with constant space.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 2. When one ends, jump to the other list's head
3. They meet at the shared node or both null
slides.narration: Step by step. First, advance both pointers. Second, when one ends, jump to the other list's head. Third, they meet at the shared node or both null.

slides.narration: The two lists merge at the node with value one and share everything after it.

slides.narration: Each pointer travels the length of both lists, so they line up and meet at the shared node.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: Two pointers start at each head. While they differ, each moves to next, or to the other list's head when it hits null. Return either.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n plus m. Space is constant.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: No intersection → both reach null together
slides.narration: Compare node references, not values; two different nodes can share a value. With no intersection, both reach null together and we return null.

bullets: Two pointers that switch to the other list after finishing travel the same distance and meet at the junction.
